title: Virtual Mentorship
thesis: A mentor that answers a visitor's question, what-should-I-do questions included, only from a bundled corpus of public-domain counsel: the visitor sees the BM25-ranked passages it read with their scores, gets one model answer that covers the question's key points and whose every numbered citation a deterministic verifier has checked against its passage, sees it refuse when retrieval is weak, and can trace every claim to its source in one click.

axes.name: Retrieval fidelity
axes.metric: Retrieval quality and scoring correctness: Recall@5 and nDCG@10 (0 to 1) on a shipped labeled query set, and the maximum absolute BM25 score difference against a reference implementation. A rater reads the retriever module and its tests, and reads the eval table on the page.
ladder: Absent: no passage is retrieved for any query.
Passages containing at least one query word are returned, ranked by a score that rises with the number of distinct query words matched.
Term weighting by inverse document frequency (TF-IDF or a later IDF-weighted scheme), with lowercase tokenization and a stopword list of at least 100 English words.

BM25 (Robertson and Zaragoza 2009, Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval) with k1 and b read from config (defaults 1.2 and 0.75), length normalized by average passage length, and the non-negative IDF variant Lucene's BM25Similarity uses, ln(1 + (N - n + 0.5) / (n + 0.5)), stated as a variant in the code.
An inverted index (term to postings of passage id and term frequency) is built once, and a query reads only the postings of its own terms; the code does not loop over every passage per query.

The tokenizer passes a shipped list of at least 30 hard cases (hyphenated words, apostrophes, numbers with units, accented letters folded to ASCII), and the Porter stemmer (Porter 1980, Program) runs on both index and query.

A labeled set of at least 30 queries with graded relevance judgments over the corpus ships with the lab, and the page recomputes Recall@5 and nDCG@10 (Jarvelin and Kekalainen 2002, ACM TOIS) from those judgments whenever k1 or b changes, so a rater who moves k1 sees the numbers change.

Scores match a named reference BM25 implementation (Lucene's BM25Similarity through Pyserini, or another stated one) within 0.0001 on every query-passage pair of the labeled set, given the same tokens, with that implementation's length quantization and constant factors reproduced; a test enforces it.
A second lexical ranker toggles on: pseudo-relevance feedback that expands the query with the top 10 terms of the top 10 passages, and the eval table shows both rankers on the same queries.

Hybrid retrieval: an in-browser dense embedding model ranks beside BM25, the two are fused by reciprocal rank fusion (Cormack, Clarke and Buettcher 2009, SIGIR), and the table shows BM25, dense, and fused results on at least 100 labeled queries.

Reference: on a BEIR dataset bundled in full (SciFact or NFCorpus; Thakur et al. 2021, NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks), the in-browser BM25 reproduces Pyserini's BM25 flat nDCG@10 from its BEIR regression page within 0.005, the in-browser dense model reproduces its own MTEB leaderboard nDCG@10 on the same dataset within 0.01, the fused ranker's nDCG@10 is published beside both, and per-query results on at least 200 of the lab's own labeled queries are published.

G0.evidence: no page exists; the hub lists mentorship as planned in labs/assets/js/config/site.config.js, and the repo holds no BM25, index, or retrieval code (a grep for bm25 finds only portfolio prose in the root index.html, line 321)

axes.name: Citation verification
axes.metric: The checks the deterministic verifier runs per citation (marker range, quote match, content-word support, numbers, negations, names), the share of citations it covers (percent), and its precision and recall (0 to 1) for the unsupported verdict on labeled claim-passage pairs drawn from real model answers. A rater reads the verifier module and its tests, and reads the verdicts on one live answer.
ladder: Absent: citations in the answer are not checked.
Every [n] marker is parsed from the answer and checked to point at one of the passages sent to the model; out-of-range and missing markers are flagged.
Every answer sentence is classed as cited or uncited, and uncited sentences are marked in the answer.
Each citation carries a verbatim quote returned by the model, checked as an exact substring of the cited passage after case and whitespace folding; each citation shows pass or fail.
Quote matching tolerates punctuation, ellipses, and up to 2 token edits by token-level alignment, and each citation reports the edit count of its match.
Support score per citation: the share of the claim's content words (stopwords removed, stemmed) found in the cited passage, with a stated threshold splitting supported, partial, and unsupported.

Fact checks per citation: every number with its unit, every negation word (from a shipped list of at least 10), and every capitalized word not at sentence start in the claim must appear in the cited passage, and a failed check names itself in the verdict.

A labeled set of at least 100 claim-passage pairs, taken from real model answers to the lab's shipped questions (not written to exercise the checks), at least 30 of them unsupported, ships with the lab; a button on the page or the node eval script recomputes the verifier's precision and recall for the unsupported verdict from it, both at least 0.75.

An in-browser natural language inference model, loaded on demand, scores entailment for each claim-passage pair as a further check, and on the labeled pairs the page shows the combined verifier's precision and recall for the unsupported verdict beside the lexical verifier's.

Answer-level citation recall and citation precision as defined in ALCE (Gao et al. 2023, EMNLP), with the in-browser entailment model as the judge in place of ALCE's (stated on the page), are shown for every answer, and the combined verifier reaches precision of at least 0.90 and recall of at least 0.85 on at least 300 labeled pairs drawn from real model answers.

Reference: on at least 500 claim-citation pairs judged by humans under the Attributable to Identified Sources protocol (Rashkin et al. 2023, Computational Linguistics), the verifier agrees with the human labels at Cohen's kappa of at least 0.75, and its errors are published, itemized by check.

G0.evidence: no page exists; the repo holds no citation parser or verifier code for this lab

axes.name: Refusal calibration
axes.metric: Refusal behavior on the lab's question file, split into answerable and off-corpus questions: the refusal rate on each half (percent) and the area under the risk-coverage curve (AURC), where coverage is the share of questions answered and risk is the share of answered questions that are off-corpus. A rater reads the refusal policy code and the eval table on the page, and asks one question the corpus cannot answer.
ladder: Absent: the mentor answers every question, whatever retrieval found.
Refuses when no passage matches any query term, and says no source was found.
Refuses when the top BM25 score is under a fixed threshold in config, and the refusal shows the top score beside the threshold.

The threshold is query-normalized: the top score is divided by the query's upper bound, the sum over its terms of each term's maximum possible contribution under the implemented scoring formula (IDF x (k1 + 1) with the classic numerator, IDF alone for Lucene 8 and later), so one threshold holds for short and long queries and for any k1.
A second signal joins the decision (the share of query terms matched by the top 3 passages), and a refusal names which signal failed.
Partial answers: when at least 1 query content term occurs in the top k passages and at least 1 occurs in none of them, the mentor answers from the passages and lists the terms found in none.
The lab's question file holds at least 40 questions, half answerable from the corpus and half not, each marked as such, and the page shows the refusal rate on each half at the shipped threshold.

A threshold slider reruns the question file live and draws the risk-coverage curve (El-Yaniv and Wiener 2010, JMLR), coverage being the share of questions answered and risk the share of answered questions that are off-corpus, with the shipped threshold marked on it and the AURC printed.
A post-answer gate: when the verifier finds under a stated share of claims supported, the answer is withheld with the reason, and the eval reports the combined pre- and post-answer policy.

A logistic regression over at least 3 query performance predictors (normalized top score, the spread of the top 10 scores as in NQC by Shtok et al. 2012, ACM TOIS, and query term coverage), fit on one half of the question file with a fixed seed or by 5-fold cross-validation, gives the probability a question is answerable; it gates after the rung-3 threshold, each refusal shows the probability beside its cutoff and every predictor's value, and the page shows the held-out expected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins and the held-out AURC.

Reference: on at least 200 questions, including adversarial unanswerables written against the corpus in the manner of SQuAD 2.0 (Rajpurkar, Jia and Liang 2018, ACL), the policy refuses at least 90% of unanswerables while answering at least 85% of answerables with key-point recall of at least 0.5 against their gold key points, published per question with its AURC.

G0.evidence: no page exists; the repo holds no refusal policy, threshold, or question file for this lab

axes.name: Model contribution
axes.metric: What the model adds over the deterministic engine: model calls per question, the share of claims by origin (model or extractive engine), and on the answerable questions of the question file each origin's verified-claim rate and key-point recall (percent). A rater asks one question, reads the ledger and the route panel, and reads the prompt-building and parsing code.
ladder: Absent: no model is called.
One model call through labs/assets/js/ai/llm.js returns an answer to the visitor's question, shown as text.
The call carries the top-k retrieved passages numbered [1] to [k] with an instruction to cite by number, and the route panel (route-panel.js) shows which route answered.
The call asks for JSON (a list of claims, each with citation numbers and a verbatim quote), and a malformed reply is repaired or rejected with the reason shown.
Offline engine: when no route answers, a deterministic extractive answer (the top sentences of the top passages, each with its citation) is composed and labeled as offline.
Exactly one model call per answered question and zero per refusal, enforced in code and shown on the page with the route and its wait for the 45-second public window.
A ledger per answer lists every claim with its origin (model or extractive engine), its citation, and its verifier verdict, with totals per origin.

Side by side: the same question answered by the extractive engine and by the model, each with its claim count and verified-claim count, and, for a question from the question file, the share of its gold key points each covers.

A stored run over the answerable questions of the question file reports, for the model and the extractive engine, key-point recall against the gold key points, verified-claim rate, citation precision, and answered share, with the model name and run date, and states the model's margin over the engine on key-point recall.
Unsupported model claims go through one deterministic repair (dropped, or reattached to another sent passage that verifies) with no second model call, and the ledger shows each drop and reattachment.

Reference: a published table across at least 3 named models (the local Ollama default, the public route model, and one own-key model) on at least 100 questions gives key-point recall, verified-claim rate, citation precision and recall, and refusal agreement per model, with the extractive engine as the baseline row.

G0.evidence: no page exists; the shared route labs/assets/js/ai/llm.js exists but nothing in this lab calls it, so no model call is made

axes.name: Answer adequacy
axes.metric: Key-point recall (percent): the share of each answerable question's gold key points that the answer covers, for the model and for the extractive engine; and the share of applied-advice sentences that cite the principle they apply (percent). A rater asks 3 questions from the question file, reads each one's gold key points and coverage readout, and reads the eval table.
ladder: Absent: no answer is produced.
An answer is produced for a typed question, from the model or the offline engine, and is shown in full.

Every question gets a type (fact, explanation, or situational advice): questions in the lab's question file carry one, a typed question is classed by a stated rule shown beside its answer, and the prompt template sends a different instruction per type, readable in the code.
Every answerable question in the question file carries 2 to 6 gold key points written from the corpus, each listing the passage ids that support it.

Each answer to a question from the question file shows which gold key points it covers, judged by content-word support of the answer against each key point at a stated threshold, with the covered share as a percent.
Answer sentences are labeled source statement or applied advice; every applied-advice sentence cites the passage whose principle it applies, and advice with no cited principle is flagged on the page.

At least 30 answerable questions in the question file are situational (a visitor's circumstance, not a lookup), and the page shows the mean key-point recall of the model's answers on them from a stored run with its date.
At least 10 answerable questions need key points from 2 or more works in the corpus, and the eval reports key-point recall on them separately.

Reference: nugget-style evaluation as in the TREC question answering and RAG tracks, on at least 200 questions with human-written key points, published per question and per model beside the extractive baseline, with the mentor's key-point recall at least 0.15 above that baseline.

A rater types one question of their own before counting, counts the views at 1440 px and 400 px, and hovers or focuses one citation.

Per-term decomposition: each score bar splits into segments, one per query term, sized by that term's BM25 contribution, with a legend keyed to the query terms.
Linked citations: hovering or focusing [n] in the answer highlights passage n and its matched quote span, and focusing a passage highlights every claim that cites it.
Verdict marks: each citation marker shows supported, partial, or unsupported by glyph and label (not color alone), and focusing it lists the checks that passed and failed.
A score distribution chart plots the top 20 scores for the query with the refusal threshold as a line, updating live as the query, k1, or b changes.

axes.name: Citation apparatus
axes.metric: Conformance of the reading and citation typography to labs/assets/css/tokens.css and a written apparatus spec: citation mark form, answer, passage and source-line registers, verdict glyphs, number setting, motion tokens, and the count of gold elements at rest. A rater inspects computed styles in devtools and counts gold elements before any interaction.
ladder: Absent: no page to style.

The page links labs/assets/css/tokens.css, the lab's CSS sets every color through var(--...) with no raw hex outside tokens.css, and a header carries the lab title and a link back to labs/index.html.

Answer, passages, and source lines are three typographic registers: the answer at a computed 16 to 18 px with a measure of 60 to 75 characters (--measure is 64ch), the passages at a computed 13 to 15 px, and each passage under a source line set at --t-stamp or smaller in --text-dim.
Citation markers are bracketed numerals [n], and scores are right-aligned tabular figures with a fixed number of decimals.

Gold is kept for the active element: at rest at most 1 element (the Ask button) computes a gold token (--accretion, --accretion-soft, --accretion-dim, or --accretion-glow) in its color, background, or border, and while a citation is focused only that citation and its passage add gold.

Every text and mark color pair the page uses passes WCAG 2.2 AA against its ground (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for score bars, verdict glyphs, and focus rings), checked with the devtools contrast readout on each of these the page shows: answer text, passage text, source line, score figure, citation marker, each verdict glyph, score bar, and focus ring; --text-faint (#424B57) is not used for readable text.

Motion uses only the shared tokens in tokens.css (--t-fast, --t-mid, --t-slow; --ease, --ease-out, --ease-in): passage highlight, citation link, and rank change reference them, and the lab's CSS and JS contain no raw millisecond duration and no cubic-bezier literal.
